correctness.rationale: PASS: For prime-power q>=3, integer d>=3, the monomial character/Krawtchouk basis identifies radial Fourier spectra with real cubics P(t) nonnegative at all integer t=0..d. Fourier inversion gives f(0)=E P(X), X~Bin(d,p), total counting mass=P(0). Averaging over Hamming isometries legitimizes radial upper bound for every positive-definite f. Let r=floor((d-1)p), theta=(d-1)p-r, Delta=(d-1)p(1-p)-theta(1-theta)>0. Cubic (d-t)(t-r)(t-r-1)>=0 on integer grid and expectation d(1-p)Delta; Lagrange expectation at 0,r,r+1,d has four nonnegative weights and w0=(1-p)Delta/[r(r+1)], proving matching upper bound T=r(r+1)/[(1-p)Delta]. Positive interpolation weights yield unique normalized P_r except theta=p (d≡2 mod q), when one quadrature weight vanishes and normalized P_r,P_{r+1} form the complete radial maximizing segment. Independent exact-rational moment/quadrature plus LP was checked for 48 (q,d) pairs (q=3,4,5,7, d=3..14), no finite test used as proof. No nonradial optimizer classification claimed.
